text:
Nihal: Heads up — after installing redwoodctl via npm on a new laptop, `redwoodctl login --profile=staging` opens the browser but the CLI never picks up the token. `redwoodctl whoami` still reports no active session.
Jen: hmm, are you on zsh or fish?
Nihal: zsh (oh-my-zsh). Also noticed it created ~/.config/redwood/config but redwoodctl is looking at ~/.redwoodrc? not consistent.
Alex: we recently added XDG support but there was a fallback order bug. Does `REDWOODCTL_CONFIG` env var help if you point it at the file?
Nihal: setting REDWOODCTL_CONFIG to ~/.config/redwood/config makes `whoami` work. But this breaks local-serve which reads profiles from ~/.redwood/profiles.json — two different locations.
DevEx Bot: documented workaround: set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG and REDWOOD_LOCAL_PROFILES to point both commands at the same directory. See https://intranet.devex/redwoodctl-config (cc @DevEx). :information_source:
Sam: rough repro steps? we should make a small test matrix (install method x shell x OS).
Nihal: repro: macOS Ventura, Node 20 via nvm, `npm i -g @redwood/cli`, zsh. Steps: npm install, run `redwoodctl login --profile=staging`, auth flow completes in browser, CLI prints "auth success", but `redwoodctl whoami` -> "not logged in". If I export REDWOODCTL_CONFIG to the xdg file, whoami shows user.
Alex: thanks — likely installer puts config in XDG but the binary's default path is older dotfile. Will push a fix to unify paths and a migration path.
Maria: also saw fish users hit a separate issue where `redwoodctl install-completion` writes to ~/.config/fish/completions but the postinstall script assumes bashrc path and errors. Might be related to how npm scripts detect shells.
Jen: for immediate workaround for Nihal: `cp ~/.config/redwood/config ~/.redwoodrc && mkdir -p ~/.redwood && cp ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json ~/.redwood/profiles.json` then `redwoodctl whoami` should work. Also you can run `redwoodctl login --profile=staging --write-config ~/.redwoodrc` (if you have that flag).
Nihal: copy worked, thanks. Will avoid npm global for now and try brew.
Alex: follow-up plan: 1) quick patch to prefer REDWOODCTL_CONFIG env var if present (hotfix), 2) unify default paths (XDG first, legacy dotfiles second) in next release, 3) add an installer test case for fish/zsh/bash completions, 4) add a one-line CLI diagnostic `redwoodctl doctor` to show which config paths it's consulting.
Sam: can we add an automated e2e in CI to run `redwoodctl login` headless against the dev-auth test client? would catch regressions.
Alex: yes — creating a ticket and assigning.
DevEx Bot: Created task RW-2314: "unify config path handling and installer completion detection" assigned to Alex, priority P2. Link: https://issues.internal/RW-2314
Nihal: awesome, thanks team. One last note: login retries felt aggressive — retry jitter was tiny and produced 429s during auth provider hiccup. If you bump backoff that should help flakiness in CI.
Alex: noted. Will tune retry/backoff and add metrics for auth retry counts.
Maria: I'll open a small PR to update postinstall scripts for fish detection.
Jen: marking this thread as resolved for now — thanks all. :thumbsup:
